title: Apple Promotes Indian-Origin Rajesh Ambati and Two Others to Engineering Vice President
excerpt: Rajesh Ambati, Louie Sanguinetti and Derek Shaeffer became vice presidents for connectivity in Apple's October promotions, as display veterans Wei Chen and John Zhong step back to adviser roles under CEO John Ternus.
body:
• Apple has promoted Indian-origin Rajesh Ambati, Louie Sanguinetti and Derek Shaeffer to vice president, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported; their work covers connectivity hardware and software.
  • Display veterans Wei Chen and John Zhong, each with roughly 30 years at Apple, are moving to more limited adviser roles, with Victor Yin now overseeing much of display development.
  • The changes are part of CEO John Ternus's reshaping of Apple: Johny Srouji's role expanded to chief hardware officer, and some hardware program managers have been laid off as management layers are removed.
  • App Store head Carson Oliver also received a vice president title, and Steve Smith has taken charge of corporate development.

Apple has promoted three engineering leaders — Rajesh Ambati, Louie Sanguinetti and Derek Shaeffer — to vice president, part of a broader series of leadership changes reported by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Their work covers connectivity hardware and software, with Sanguinetti's contributions to wireless hardware stretching back decades, according to MacRumors.

Ambati was a senior director of software engineering and Sanguinetti a director of wireless hardware engineering before the promotions, which came in Apple's October cycle. The appointments are promotions from within to cover positions vacated by executives who are retiring, not a round of firings, according to AppleInsider.

"Their work covers connectivity hardware and software, with Sanguinetti's contributions to wireless hardware stretching back decades, according to MacRumors ."

The display handover

The larger change sits in displays. Wei Chen and John Zhong, each with approximately 30 years at the company, are taking on more limited responsibilities as advisers. Victor Yin now oversees much of Apple's display development after years of preparation under the two men, and Gurman describes their eventual departures as part of a succession process that has been underway for several years. Chen had taken over Touch ID in 2023 when its previous head retired.

Yin, as vice president of display hardware, has been mentored by Chen and Zhong for some years specifically to take over at least part of their roles — a managed changeover rather than a sudden exit.

Ternus reshapes the top

The appointments follow Apple's decision to expand Johny Srouji's role to chief hardware officer, bringing hardware engineering and hardware technologies under his leadership. A subsequent reorganisation of product development sought to improve coordination between the teams designing Apple's chips and its devices.

Gurman also reports that some hardware program managers have been laid off in recent weeks as Srouji and CEO John Ternus remove management layers and reduce the number of positions between engineers and senior leadership, in an effort to accelerate product development. Elsewhere at Apple, App Store head Carson Oliver has received a vice president title, and Steve Smith has taken charge of corporate development after its previous leader retired.

Why it matters

For the diaspora reader, Ambati's elevation is the headline inside the headline: connectivity — the radios, networking and software that link every iPhone, Mac and accessory — now has an Indian-origin vice president in a company where senior engineering leadership has been steadily internationalising. The pattern of the reshuffle is consistent: promote long-serving specialists, hand retiring veterans an adviser bridge, and flatten the layers in between. Whether that speeds up Apple's product cycle, as Ternus intends, will show in the next two release seasons.
